title: Vatican announces November papal trip to South America, including Peru
text:
Vatican announces November papal trip to South America, including Peru
LAX Leader
Pope Leo XIV will make his first apostolic journey to South America as pope from Nov. 6-17, visiting ten cities across Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, the Vatican announced on Aug. 5.
The itinerary includes stops in Montevideo, Paysandú and Florida in Uruguay; Buenos Aires, Córdoba and Luján in Argentina; and Lima, Chiclayo, Cusco and Pucallpa in Peru. This marks Pope Leo's return to the continent where he previously served as an Augustinian missionary and later bishop of Chiclayo before his election as pope.
In Uruguay—the least religious country in Latin America with Christians comprising only 44% of the population according to Pew Research Center—the visit will begin in Montevideo. The capital is home to major Catholic sites such as the National Shrine of the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Cardinal Daniel Sturla of Montevideo said, "Almost 40 years ago, we experienced the unforgettable visit of St. John Paul II. Now we welcome Pope Leo with enormous anticipation. It is a joy for the Church, but also for all of Uruguay." The papal route continues through Paysandú—known for its Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary—and Florida’s National Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three.
The second leg takes Pope Leo XIV to Argentina—the homeland of Pope Francis—where about 58% identify as Catholic according to Pew Research Center. In Buenos Aires he is expected to meet President Javier Milei, who described it as "an event of enormous spiritual and institutional significance for our country and for all Argentines." Other stops include Córdoba’s Jesuit Block—a UNESCO World Heritage site—and Luján’s Shrine of Our Lady.
The final portion brings him back to Peru where he was a missionary beginning in 1985 before serving as bishop until his transfer to Rome in 2023. In Lima he will be welcomed by President Keiko Fujimori following her July victory declaration. The trip includes Chiclayo—where local ties are strong due to his former role—Cusco with its Inca heritage, and Pucallpa on the Ucayali River known for Catholic outreach efforts.
The Diocese of Chiclayo celebrated news of the journey, saying it would bring "a message of faith, hope, and closeness to millions of Peruvians." The diocese added: "It will be a historic visit that will unite us as a people and as a Church... With joy and hope, we prepare to welcome the Successor of Peter and experience this time together."

In Uruguay—the least religious country in Latin America with Christians comprising only 44% of the population according to Pew Research Center—the visit will begin in Montevideo. In Buenos Aires he is expected to meet President Javier Milei, who described it as "an event of enormous spiritual and institutional significance for our country and for all Argentines."
